title: Expose the cosh magnetization bias and vanishing-field cost of the symmetrization shortcut
statement: For mu_h(sigma) proportional to mu_0(sigma) exp(h M(sigma)), mixing mu_h with its global spin flip gives nu_h(sigma)=mu_0(sigma) cosh(hM)/E_mu0 cosh(hM), not the zero-field law. On an edgeless n-vertex graph, a=tanh h and the event |M|>=na/2 give TV(nu_h,mu_0)>=1-8/(n a^2). TV<=1/2 therefore requires n tanh^2 h<=16, hence positive h=O(n^-1/2). In the supplied explicit Chen field-dynamics parameters, this vanishing field gap makes log T_FD=Omega(n^2). This rules out that proposed symmetrization/localization shortcut under its given cost, not all zero-field RNC algorithms.

costs: Outside a required EvenCore subroutine, rational coins use L=ceil(log2(8 max(1,m)/epsilon)) unbiased bits each and the comparison bU<a*2^L. Per-edge error is <2^-L and the union error is <=epsilon/8; O(B+L)-bit arithmetic is charged. An epsilon/2 core sample, deterministic NC connectivity, fair component signs and the rational completion coins yield full-joint error <=epsilon.
